title: Private deployments — VPC & on‑prem deployment best practices and day‑2 ops
author: Aisha Patel
summary: This page consolidates Redwood Inference best practices for private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It covers reference architectures, packaging recommendations, day‑2 operations, upgrade and rollback procedures, and the customer requirements library. Intended for solutions engineers, platform operators, and customer SREs.
body:
Contents:
- Introduction and scope
- Reference architectures (VPC and on‑prem)
- On‑prem packaging and install artifacts
- Day‑2 operations checklist and runbook links
- Upgrade & rollback procedures (canary and full upgrades)
- Customer requirements library (networking, security, capacity)
- Ownership, SLOs, and escalation paths

1. Introduction and scope
This guide describes production‑grade deployment patterns for Redwood Private which supports two primary modes: VPC (customer cloud account with private peering to Redwood control plane) and On‑prem (air‑gapped or partially networked installations using the on‑prem package).

Target audience: solutions engineers, eng‑platform, customer SREs, and infra teams responsible for provisioning, day‑2 operations, and upgrades.

Constraints: specific cloud IAM/KMS guidance is provided at a high level; customers should map recommendations to their corporate controls.

2. Reference architectures
High level goals: isolate customer data, provide predictable latency for model inference, enable secure key management, and support graceful capacity scaling.

2.1 VPC reference architecture (recommended for most customers)
- Components:
  - Customer VPC with private subnets for inference nodes and control plane egress endpoints
  - PrivateLink / VPC Peering to Redwood control plane (control plane only; inference data can remain in customer VPC)
  - Autoscaling GPU node pools (k8s node groups or managed GPU pools)
  - Internal NLB/ALB for customer traffic with mTLS termination at edge if required
  - KMS integration for customer keys (via cloud KMS or HSM)
  - Private ECR/ACR (or equivalent) for secure image hosting in customer account
- Networking requirements (minimum):
  - NAT/egress for OS updates (or allowlist Redwood update endpoints if fully restricted)
  - Reserved /24 for internal service endpoint mapping
  - 10.0.0.0/16 recommended for new deployments to avoid collisions
- Security controls:
  - IAM least privilege roles for node bootstrap and image pull
  - RBAC mapping between k8s and Redwood service accounts
  - Audit logging to customer SIEM (CloudWatch / Stackdriver / Azure Monitor)

2.2 On‑prem reference architecture (air‑gapped or regulated environments)
- Components:
  - On‑prem appliance (OVA/container bundle) deployable to customer hypervisor or k8s cluster
  - Local artifact registry (Nexus/Artifactory) and package repository mirror
  - Air‑gap sync appliance for periodic packaging updates (pulls signed bundles from Redwood when allowed)
  - HSM/KMS on‑prem integration or KMIP proxy
  - Local observability export (Prometheus pushgateway to a local Prometheus/Thanos)
- Physical requirements:
  - Minimum 3 control nodes + GPU worker nodes (see Capacity table below)
  - Dedicated management network for orchestration and node management
- Security controls:
  - Signed image verification during install
  - Local attestations and signed manifests

3. On‑prem packaging and install artifacts
Redwood on‑prem distribution is delivered as a signed bundle with the following artifacts: redwood-package-{version}.tar.gz (signed SHA256 manifest), kube-manifests/{component}.yaml (templated manifests), images.txt (registry:tag list for preloading), helm-chart (optional) for customers running Helm.

Install flow (high level):
1. Validate preflight checklist (disk, CPU, GPU, network reachability) — see section 5.
2. Upload signed bundle to local artifact registry.
3. Preload container images onto nodes or configure registry mirror.
4. Apply kube manifests / Helm chart with environment values.
5. Run smoke tests (see smoke test CLI example below).

Sample preflight CLI (run on bootstrap host):
# Verify GPU drivers and NVIDIA DCGM
sudo ./tools/check-nvidia.sh --expect 1
# Validate image checksum
sha256sum -c redwood-package-{version}.manifest

Smoke test (after install):
curl -s --cacert /etc/redwood/ca.pem -X POST https://localhost:8443/v1/health | jq .

3.1 Packaging recommendations for customers
- Mirror images to local registry with immutability tags (avoid :latest)
- Use signed manifests verified at bootstrap
- Keep image TTLs aligned with customer patch cycles (by default we publish quarterly security bundles)

4. Day‑2 operations (runbook summary)
This section summarizes the operational tasks that recur during lifetime of a private deployment. Detailed runbooks are linked in related_pages.

4.1 Monitoring & alerts (recommended thresholds)
- Node GPU utilization alert: trigger > 90% sustained for 5 min
- KV cache hit rate drop: drop below 80% for 10m => investigate workload pattern change
- Latency SLO: p95 inference latency > 250ms (for 2–8k token workloads on XX GPU profile) => page oncall
- Disk pressure: > 70% used on any control node => schedule capacity add

4.2 Backups & disaster recovery
- Redis/KV periodic snapshots: daily, retain 14 days
- Model artifacts: replicate to object store (S3/MinIO) and verify with a weekly checksum job
- Control plane DB: nightly logical backups with PITR where supported

4.3 Routine tasks
- Certificate rotation: every 90 days (automated scripts provided)
- Image patching: monthly critical, quarterly regular
- Capacity review: monthly, or triggered when p95 latency increases > 10%

4.4 Escalation and runbook links
- Primary alert triage: customer SRE -> Redwood SE (redwood-support@redwood.ai) -> Redwood oncall
- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-runbook-2026-03-10 for step-by-step incident procedures

5. Upgrade and rollback procedures
Upgrades must be planned and validated. We support two upgrade strategies: canary and rolling (full) upgrade.

Preupgrade checklist (required):
- Backup control plane DB
- Snapshot KV cache and model stores
- Verify smoke test baseline (store a copy of baseline outputs for 3 canonical prompts)
- Confirm rollback window and maintenance window with customer

5.1 Canary upgrade (recommended for high-risk changes)
1. Create a new release tag (e.g. vX.Y.Z-canary-<date>) and push signed bundle
2. Deploy new bundle to a small subset of worker nodes (5–10% or 1 node minimum)
3. Route 1–2% of traffic to canary via traffic routing policy; maintain mirroring of production traffic for log/metric parity
4. Monitor for 30–60 minutes against Canary acceptance criteria: error rate increase <= 0.5% absolute, p95 latency delta <= +15%, no model output regressions for canonical prompts (>90% similarity by eval metric)
5. If acceptance criteria met, start progressive rollout in 10–25% increments with 15–30 minute observation windows. If failed, follow immediate rollback.

5.2 Rolling full upgrade (for low risk/security patches)
1. Drain one control or worker node at a time
2. Apply patch and run smoke tests
3. Bring node back and wait for stabilization (10 min of healthy metrics)
4. Continue until all nodes upgraded

5.3 Rollback procedure
- Trigger conditions: Canary acceptance failure, major errors, security regression
- Steps: 1) Stop traffic to affected nodes (failover to previous version pools) 2) Redeploy previous signed bundle from archived artifact store 3) Restore control plane DB snapshot if schema changes were applied — only if required 4) Revalidate baseline smoke tests and resume traffic
- Time targets: aim to rollback within the agreed maintenance window; emergency rollback SLA is 2 hours for high-severity failures

Compatibility table (excerpt):
Component | Forward compatible | Notes
--- | ---: | ---
Control plane DB migrations | No | Use blue/green for major schema changes
Worker runtime | Yes | Backward compatible for model serving in 90% cases
KV cache format | No | Requires migration script during upgrade window

6. Customer requirements library (summary)
This section is a condensed, operational customer requirements checklist for sales/solutions intake. Full library pages exist as separate docs referenced in related_pages.

6.1 Networking
- Dedicated VPC/subnet for Redwood nodes
- Allowlist for Redwood control plane IPs (if not using PrivateLink)
- MTU >= 9000 for RDMA setups (recommended for NVLink/NCCL)

6.2 Security & compliance
- KMS/HSM availability for key wrapping
- Audit logging forwarding to SIEM
- SOC2 / ISO27001 requirements documented and satisfied by contract

6.3 Capacity and performance
- Minimum GPU profile: 4x A10G or equivalent for small production (8 concurrent streams)
- Baseline throughput targets provided during scoping; customers must supply expected RPS, average token length, and acceptable p95 latency

6.4 Packaging & install
- Customer provides artifact registry for on‑prem images
- Admin user for bootstrap with sudo and ability to configure iptables

7. Ownership, SLOs, and communications
- Document owner: Aisha Patel (eng‑platform)
- Support path: redwood-support@redwood.ai (primary), oncall@redwood.ai (escalation)
- SLOs for Private deployments (customer contract configurable): Control plane API availability: 99.9% monthly; p95 inference latency targets: defined per deployment profile (example profile: small = 250ms p95; medium = 150ms p95)

8. Appendix
8.1 Useful commands
- Fetch logs from node: kubectl -n redwood logs --selector=component=worker -c inference --tail=500
- Trigger KV cache snapshot: curl -X POST "https://localhost:8443/v1/admin/kv/snapshot" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

8.2 Further reading
- See related pages for deep dive runbooks, packaging guides, and the full customer requirements library.
